Class DefaultAtom<T>

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.substrate.core.atom.DefaultAtom<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the type of value held by this atom
All Implemented Interfaces:
Atom<T>
public class DefaultAtom<T> extends Object implements Atom<T>
Default Atom handle: a single value at a key, read and replaced under a staleness token so concurrent writers detect each other.

    • compareAndSet

      public boolean compareAndSet(Snapshot<T> expected, T data, Duration ttl)
      Description copied from interface: Atom
      Atomically sets the value of this atom only if its current token matches the one carried by expected. On success the TTL is reset and subscribers are notified; on failure nothing is written and no notification is sent.

      A false return is retryable — another writer won the race, so re-read and try again. AtomExpiredException is terminal — the atom is gone and retrying cannot succeed. 

      Snapshot<Session> current = atom.get();
Session next = current.value().withCount(current.value().count() + 1);
while (!atom.compareAndSet(current, next, Duration.ofHours(1))) {
  current = atom.get();
  next = current.value().withCount(current.value().count() + 1);
}
      Specified by:
      compareAndSet in interface Atom<T>
      Parameters:
      expected - the snapshot this write is conditioned on
      data - the new value to store
      ttl - the new time-to-live for this atom
      Returns:
      true if the write was committed, false if another writer changed the atom first

    • delete

      public void delete()
      Description copied from interface: Atom
      Explicitly deletes this atom, immediately expiring its lease.

      After deletion, subsequent calls to Atom.set(T, Duration), Atom.get(), and Atom.touch(Duration) will behave as though the atom's TTL has elapsed.

      Specified by:
      delete in interface Atom<T>

    • subscribe

      public BlockingSubscription<Snapshot<T>> subscribe()
      Description copied from interface: Atom
      Subscribes from the current state using a blocking pull model. The first next() call returns the current snapshot (if the atom exists); subsequent next() calls block until the next Atom.set(T, Duration) occurs.
      Specified by:
      subscribe in interface Atom<T>
      Returns:
      a BlockingSubscription that yields Snapshot instances

    • subscribe

      public BlockingSubscription<Snapshot<T>> subscribe(Snapshot<T> lastSeen)
      Description copied from interface: Atom
      Subscribes from a known baseline using a blocking pull model. If the atom's current token differs from lastSeen.token(), the first next() call returns the current snapshot immediately; otherwise the first next() blocks until the next change.
      Specified by:
      subscribe in interface Atom<T>
      Parameters:
      lastSeen - the baseline to compare against, or null for equivalent behavior to Atom.subscribe()
      Returns:
      a BlockingSubscription that yields Snapshot instances
